questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Kuwait about 17,818 square kilometres; Qatar about 11,437 square kilometres; Lebanon about 10,452 square kilometres; Palestine about 6,020 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: True or false: “The capital city of Kuwait is Tehran.”

hints.nudge: Read the statement slowly. Does it match what the article says, or has one word been swapped for another?
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kuwait article, or on the Atlas.

questions.proof: The capital city of Kuwait is Kuwait City.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Kuwait?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Kuwait is the Kuwaiti dinar.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Kuwait?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kuwait article.

questions.proof: Arabic is mostly spoken in Kuwait but English is widespread among Kuwaitis (residents of Kuwait).

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Kuwait on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Kuwait on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
